End User Licence Agreement — Football Team Simulator

Draft. Have a lawyer read this before publishing it.

Note that on Steam, Google Play and the App Store the store's own standard licence applies by default, and a custom EULA is optional. It is worth having one mainly for the online conduct rules, which the store terms do not cover.

1. The agreement

This agreement is between you and Fabio Casarini ("we", "us"), the developer of Football Team Simulator ("the Game"). By installing or playing the Game you accept it. If you do not, do not install or play it.

2. Licence

We grant you a personal, non-exclusive, non-transferable licence to install and play the Game for your own non-commercial use, on the devices permitted by the store you obtained it from.

3. What you may not do

You may not: sell, rent or sublicense the Game; reverse-engineer, decompile or disassemble it, except to the extent that applicable law expressly permits this despite this clause; remove or alter any copyright notice; or use the Game to break the law.

4. Online play and conduct

If you create an account to play online, you are responsible for what happens under it and for keeping your password to yourself.

When playing online you agree not to:

  • run more than one account in order to gain an advantage, in particular to play accounts

against each other or feed one from another;

  • arrange results, or make transfers whose purpose is to move value between accounts

rather than to improve a team;

  • use software that modifies, automates or interferes with the Game or its servers;
  • choose a club, coach or display name that is offensive, that impersonates someone, or

that infringes a trademark;

  • harass other players.

We may suspend or close an account that does these things. We would rather design the game so that cheating gains nothing than police it, which is why the automatic checks exist — but the ability to intervene remains.

5. Fair-play measures

To keep competition fair the Game records a hashed form of the network address accounts connect from, flags transfers priced far away from a player's market value, limits how quickly certain actions can be repeated, and lets players report each other. What is recorded and for how long is set out in the Privacy Policy.

6. Your content

Names you choose and the teams you build remain yours. You grant us the licence needed to display them to other players in leagues, standings and the leaderboard, which is what makes online play work.

7. Availability

The Game's online features depend on servers we operate. We do not promise they will always be available, and we may change, suspend or discontinue online features. The single-player career does not depend on our servers and will keep working offline.

8. Fictional content

Every club, competition, player and coach in the Game is fictional and procedurally generated. Any resemblance to a real club, competition or person is coincidental. The Game is not affiliated with, endorsed by or licensed by any football club, league or governing body.

9. No warranty, and limits on liability

The Game is provided "as is", without warranties beyond those that cannot lawfully be excluded. Nothing in this agreement limits our liability for death or personal injury caused by negligence, for fraud, or for anything else that the law does not permit us to limit. Subject to that, our total liability is limited to the amount you paid for the Game.

If you are a consumer in the European Union or the United Kingdom, you keep your statutory rights, and nothing here reduces them.

10. Termination

The licence ends if you break this agreement. You may end it at any time by deleting the Game and, if you have one, your account.

11. Law

This agreement is governed by Italian law. If you are a consumer, you may bring proceedings in the courts of your own country of residence, and you keep the protection of the mandatory consumer law that applies there.
